assumptions.text: Tool catalogue and tool maintenance are one context (inventory): the same volunteer drives both, 'Tool' (kind) and 'Item' (unit) are two terms in one model, and nothing shifts meaning between adding a tool and retiring an item. Split later if a separate catalogue editor appears.
Stripe is an adapter inside fees (and membership for the joining fee), not a wrapper context: the storm shows one Stripe event and no Stripe vocabulary of its own.
Lending owns item availability (available / reserved / on loan); inventory owns item condition and lifecycle (in maintenance / retired) and tells lending which items exist and are fit to lend.
The spreadsheet and paper book are imported once and retired; they are not a live legacy context on the map.
Fees and membership both record card payments but fees owns the member's balance; the membership fee is not part of the balance that blocks borrowing.

Lending owns the borrowing-eligibility rule (membership current, balance zero, no overdue, fewer than three out) and the member-standing read model. Two of the four facts are lending's own state; discover N2 says lending consumes the answer; discover Q3 and Q4, which change the rule, are lending questions.

Lending obtains 'membership current' and 'balance zero' by direct read from membership and fees at check-out, not by a locally maintained projection - chosen for one Postgres, a modular monolith, two part-time devs and C2 (no babysitting). Mechanism, not boundary; connect confirms.

open_questions.text: Does an unpaid membership renewal count as 'owing' for borrowing purposes, or only late and damage fees?
Should the catalogue (public browsing of tool kinds) be split from maintenance if a member-facing editor or a second volunteer role appears?

Does the coordinator need a list of everyone currently blocked from borrowing (not just a per-member check at the desk)? If yes, lending needs a maintained standing projection rather than a read at check-out.
Must the Saturday desk check items out when the network or another part of the system is down?

notes_for_downstream.text: Sharpens discover N1: 'Item' means an availability status (available, reserved, on loan) inside lending, but a physical condition and lifecycle (fit, in maintenance, retired) inside inventory. Two meanings, two canvases; the glossary carries both.

inventory and membership are ISH 'merge'-class modules (own language, no standalone product); lending and fees are candidates. At 1-3 deployables expect a modular monolith with at most a separate scheduled worker.

Card payment adapter (Stripe) is called from two contexts (fees for late/damage fees, membership for the joining fee). Either share one thin adapter or route the membership fee through fees - decide at connect.

Eligibility has one owner: lending. Membership and fees are upstream suppliers of one fact each; lending is the customer. Connect: prefer a synchronous read at this scale; move to a subscribed projection only if fees or membership becomes a separate deployable, if a cross-member 'who is blocked' list is required (Q3), or if the desk must work degraded (Q4). Define: the member-standing entry belongs to lending, with membership-current and fee-balance as inbound.

Narrows understand cap-membership, which lists 'member standing' under Membership: membership owns membership status; lending owns standing and the borrow decision. Resolves discover H2 and closes understand N2 / discover N2.

subdomains.name: Membership
subdomains.description: Joining, concession approval, the annual fee, the 12-month term and lapsing.
subdomains.rationale: Closed by the pivotal event membership-started; the coordinator (concession) and the member drive it; it holds the GDPR-sensitive contact details and proof (C4).

subdomains.name: Inventory
subdomains.description: What tools exist as kinds, which physical items belong to each, their condition, inspection, repair and retirement.
subdomains.rationale: One actor (maintenance volunteer) owns every fact about a tool's existence and condition; 'Item' here means a physical unit with a condition, not a thing on loan.

subdomains.name: Lending
subdomains.description: Reserving, checking out, renewing, reminding, going overdue and returning items, under the 14-day / three-item / no-overdue rules.
subdomains.rationale: Two pivotal events (item-checked-out, item-returned) bound it; its words (loan, reservation, due date) appear nowhere else; its rules are the ones the library will keep tuning.

subdomains.name: Fees
subdomains.description: Late-fee accrual, damage charges, waivers, the member's balance and taking payment for it.
subdomains.rationale: Closed by the pivotal event fee-paid; only this part may change what a member owes; it is where Stripe is adapted (C1).

bounded_contexts.name: Membership

terms.meaning_here: a person with contact details, a member number, a rate (standard or concession) and a term that expires

bounded_contexts.rationale: Its own language (member, concession, term) and its own data; a module inside the monolith at this scale.

bounded_contexts.name: Inventory

terms.meaning_here: one asset-tagged physical unit with a condition and a lifecycle (fit, in maintenance, retired)
a catalogue kind with replacement value, safety notes and induction flag; owns its items

bounded_contexts.rationale: The maintenance volunteer's world; nobody else changes a tool's existence or condition.

bounded_contexts.name: Lending

terms.meaning_here: a lendable unit with an availability (available, reserved, on loan); condition is not modelled here
a borrower identified by member number with a standing (may borrow or not) - no contact details

bounded_contexts.rationale: The core of the library: the rules members and volunteers argue about live here.

bounded_contexts.name: Fees

terms.meaning_here: an account holder with a balance in pence; nothing else about the person

bounded_contexts.rationale: Money: its own ledger language, the Stripe adapter behind it, and the only place a balance changes.

relationships.description: At check-out lending asks membership whether the membership is current (memberId -> current until); lending also consumes membership-started / membership-lapsed to know who exists. Lending is the customer and can ask for fields; contact details and concession proof never cross.
At check-out lending asks fees for the member's balance (memberId -> pence owed); it never reads the ledger. Lending is the customer of that answer; fees keeps the ledger model private.
Fees accrues on loan-overdue (loanId, daysLate, item replacement value cap) and stops on item-returned; fees is a customer of what lending publishes and can ask for fields it needs.
Lending learns which items exist and are fit to lend from item-tagged, item-repaired, item-failed-inspection and item-retired; it never edits condition.
A return with damage noted (item-returned.condition) is what triggers an inspection; inventory needs the condition note and the loan reference in that event.
A failed inspection after a loan lets the coordinator charge damage up to the tool's replacement value; fees needs itemId, fault and replacement value from inventory.

context_map_mermaid:
flowchart LR
  membership["Membership"]
  inventory["Inventory"]
  lending["Lending"]
  fees["Fees"]
  membership -->|"R1 customer-supplier"| lending
  fees -->|"R2 customer-supplier"| lending
  lending -->|"R3 customer-supplier"| fees
  inventory -->|"R4 published-language"| lending
  lending -->|"R5 customer-supplier"| inventory
  inventory -->|"R6 customer-supplier"| fees

plain_words.what: We cut the library into four parts, each a place where one word keeps one meaning (a bounded context): membership, inventory, lending, fees.
plain_words.decided: Four contexts, six relationships. Lending is the middle: it owns 'may this member borrow?' and asks membership and fees for the two facts it does not hold. Card payments are an adapter inside fees, not a part of their own.
plain_words.assumed: That tool catalogue and tool maintenance belong together (same volunteer, same tools), and that 'item' means availability to lending but condition to inventory.
plain_words.riskiest: If the who-may-borrow rule does not belong in lending, the check-out flow, the canvases and the contracts after this all point the wrong way.

decisions.question: Which context owns 'may this member borrow right now?'

options.summary: Lending keeps a local member-standing read model built from membership and fees events and decides alone at check-out.
pros: Lending answers with no call out; survives membership or fees being down
A cross-member 'who is blocked' list is cheap
cons: A projection table, handlers for six event types and a rebuild path - real machinery for two part-time devs (C2)
If handlers run async, cash paid at the desk then borrowing in the same visit can show a stale balance (I3)
risks: A projection is the thing that needs babysitting; drift goes unnoticed until someone who owes money borrows

options.summary: Membership owns standing, consumes loan and fee events, and publishes standing-changed for lending to obey.
pros: Matches cap-membership as understand wrote it ('member standing')
One place a volunteer asks about a member
cons: Membership must consume seven loan and fee events it has no business in
Lending calls membership which depends on lending: a cycle
Two of the four facts are already lending's own state
risks: This is the boundary line organise and every contract inherit; reversing it later re-runs six steps

options.summary: Lending queries membership and fees synchronously inside the check-out request; nothing is duplicated.
pros: Two queries, no new table, no handlers, no rebuild; always exact
Fits C3 (one Postgres) and the modular-monolith preference
cons: Runtime coupling: if fees or membership becomes its own deployable the desk hot path gains a network hop
Cannot list everyone who is blocked without scanning
risks: Cheap to undo: add the projection later, owner unchanged

decisions.rationale: Lending owns the rule (high confidence): two of the four facts are its own state, discover N2 says it consumes the answer, and every open question that changes the rule is a lending question. The mechanism is a direct read at check-out rather than a projection (medium): at one Postgres and two part-time developers, six event handlers and a rebuild path buy nothing a single database does not already give.
would_flip_if: fees or membership is put in a separate deployable by organise
someone needs 'who is blocked right now' as a list, not a per-member check
the Saturday desk must check items out while the network or another part is down
